paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when trouble is closing in, you can run straight to the LORD with everything you've got. David doesn't tidy up his prayer first. He just says, "Hear, O LORD, my righteous plea; listen to my cry" (Psalm 17:1). He prays like a man who is SURE God will answer, because he says so himself: "I call on You, O God, for You will answer me" (Psalm 17:6).

Then look at what he asks for. He wants to be kept "as the apple of Your eye" and hidden "in the shadow of Your wings" (Psalm 17:8). That's a man who knows he can't handle the lion alone, and he's okay with that. I spent years in a drawer pretending I was fine, so trust me, asking for shelter beats acting tough. David also says God saves "those who seek refuge from their foes" (Psalm 17:7), and that's the people who run to Him.

The enemies in this psalm have their portion in this life, but David looks past it. He says, "As for me, I will behold Your face in righteousness; when I awake, I will be satisfied in Your presence" (Psalm 17:15). So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery, baker: the best thing you can ask God for is HIM. Bring Him your fears, bring Him your mess, and let Him be the one who satisfies.
